jobs.title: 道の下の分岐
jobs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: one environment or scene illustration for the original exploration game "Ash Estuary"; wide landscape, approximately 16:9, edge-to-edge, opaque background.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved STYLE reference B. Match its actual fine pen contours, soft watercolor washes, restrained realistic observation, subtle warm paper grain, and material detail. It is a style reference; do not copy its water gate or net yard into a different location. If Image 2 is supplied it is a LOCATION/OBJECT continuity reference for this scene, not a second art style.
Art direction: Quiet, beautiful, slightly uneasy coastal life. Hand-drawn pen and pale watercolor, readable space, irregular fine lines, restrained cross-hatching, delicate gray-blue atmospheric distance. Chalk-white and warm-ivory limestone, slate-gray water and sky, muted moss and blue-green, weathered brown wood and small rust accents. Soft overcast daylight, legible shadows, no crushed black or saturated cinema grading. Keep the detailed observational character of reference B rather than flattening it or switching to an oil painting.
World and visual invariants: Small preindustrial coastal settlement; ordinary human-scale architecture and maintenance. Labor and everyday materials carry the story. Memory stones have no visible readable memories or supernatural glow. No ghosts, flashbacks inside stones, restored memories, giant castles, modern machinery, monsters, fighting, magical birds, bodily corrosion, or apocalyptic destruction. No readable words, numerals, labels, arrows, captions, UI, border or watermark. Written records use indistinct pen strokes. Avoid hero poses; named character designs are not fixed, so people are small figures or cropped hands without distinctive faces.
Scene/backdrop: A small maintenance space underneath the pale paved path at the southern sluice in Image 1. Salt-worn white limestone, a shallow fork of stone-lined water channels, a plain movable wooden diversion board and a disused narrow branch. A thin white deposit bends into the old branch. This is modest hand-maintained water infrastructure, not a cathedral, laboratory or fantasy dungeon.
Subject and framing: Observational medium close view from the stone maintenance opening. A coiled inspection rope and a small practical oil lantern sit near the opening; the timber board and deposits are clearly readable in the midground. A cropped cloth sleeve or hand may steady the rope, without showing a face.
Lighting: Diffuse gray daylight from the maintenance opening, with a very small warm practical lantern accent, retaining the pale watercolor palette and fine pen detail of B.
Narrative constraints: The discovery is ONLY a physical diversion of flow. No magical energy or equation proving the efficacy of powder; no readable memory. The overlying paved path is not yet demolished, and the unused channel has not yet been blocked. The gate construction uses the same stone and wood as Image 1.

jobs.prompt:

Asset type: one environment or scene illustration for the original exploration game "Ash Estuary"; wide landscape, approximately 16:9, edge-to-edge, opaque background.
Input images: Image 1 is BOTH the EDIT TARGET and the approved style reference B. Preserve its viewpoint, estuary, buildings, stone sluice, cistern, metal net frames, overcast light and pen-and-watercolor treatment. Change only the state of the white path and the nearby work activity described below.
Art direction: Quiet, beautiful, slightly uneasy coastal life. Hand-drawn pen and pale watercolor, readable space, irregular fine lines, restrained cross-hatching, delicate gray-blue atmospheric distance. Chalk-white and warm-ivory limestone, slate-gray water and sky, muted moss and blue-green, weathered brown wood and small rust accents. No readable words, numerals, labels, arrows, captions, UI, border or watermark. Written records use indistinct pen strokes. Avoid hero poses; named character designs are not fixed, so people are small figures or cropped hands without distinctive faces.
Edit request: Show the same southern water gate after twelve hours of manual repair that required lifting part of the white paving. A modest segment of the foreground path is now opened with pale slabs stacked beside it; the opened section exposes a small old drain that has been filled with stone. The route is visibly interrupted and a plain handcart is stopped before the opening. A small anonymous work figure carries a bundled net along the remaining edge.
Invariants: Keep the sluice standing and its original masonry, water level, cistern, metal net racks, buildings, coastline, framing and quiet daylight unchanged. There is no flood, catastrophic collapse, new bridge, glow, new castle or miracle. The repair itself did not create extra powder or already choose which district to protect. No outcome such as a saved cistern or damaged net racks is asserted in this image.
